pullRequest.title: fix(apply): recover stuck preparing drafts and skip open-draft companies
pullRequest.body:
## Summary

**What this fixes, in plain terms:** if an unattended `npm run auto-prepare` run was killed part-way through a draft (a log-off, a shutdown, Task Scheduler stopping it), that application stayed "being tailored" (`preparing`) forever. It kept taking a slot in the review queue, so after a few interruptions every run reported "queue full" and quietly stopped producing drafts. Also, a company that already had a draft waiting from an earlier run could get a second one.

Now:

1. **Stuck drafts are cleaned up.** When a run is allowed to go ahead, it first moves any application that has been `preparing` for more than 30 minutes to `failed`, with a note telling the owner to start a new application to try again. This happens before the queue is counted, so the stuck row no longer blocks anything. Each one gets an `autoprepare.recovered` entry in the audit log (the permanent record of every change) under the `scheduler` actor. No other status is touched, and nothing is approved, filled or submitted.
2. **One open draft per company, across runs.** A job is skipped when its company already has an application in `preparing` or `review`, from any earlier run. The existing "one per company in this run" check and the post-submission cool-down both still apply.

### How it works

- [ApplicationRepository.failStalePreparing](server/src/persistence/application-repository.ts#L83-L93) is one `UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'preparing' AND updated_at < cutoff RETURNING id, job_id`. `updated_at` marks when preparing started (`create` and `regenerate` both set it, and nothing touches it again until tailoring ends).
- [ApplicationRepository.hasOpenDraftAtCompany](server/src/persistence/application-repository.ts#L95-L104) matches the company case- and whitespace-insensitively, the same way the service's in-run check does.
- [AutoPrepareService.run](server/src/services/apply/auto-prepare-service.ts#L70) calls [recoverStalePreparing](server/src/services/apply/auto-prepare-service.ts#L109-L118) after the setup, resume, kill-switch and feature-switch gates, and before counting the queue. [skipReason](server/src/services/apply/auto-prepare-service.ts#L130) adds the cross-run company check between the in-run check and the submission gap.

### Open questions, decided

- **Should the server's start-up also recover stale drafts?** Not in this change. Recovery happens at the start of each auto-prepare run. Issue #15's on-demand button runs the same service inside the server, so the server gets the clean-up that way without a second implementation.
- **Is 30 minutes right?** Yes. It is almost 4x the ~8-minute worst case seen in the PR #12 review, so a slow but live draft is not failed. It is one named constant ([STALE_PREPARING_MS](server/src/services/apply/auto-prepare-service.ts#L47-L52)).
- **Assumption:** recovery runs only when a run is allowed to go ahead. With the feature off, the kill switch on or setup unfinished, the run still exits before touching any row, so "off" keeps meaning off. A test covers this.

### Changed files

- [server/src/persistence/application-repository.ts:83-104](server/src/persistence/application-repository.ts#L83-L104): the two queries.
- [server/src/services/apply/auto-prepare-service.ts:47-52, 70, 109-118, 130](server/src/services/apply/auto-prepare-service.ts#L47-L130): the threshold, the recovery step and the extra skip check.
- [server/test/auto-prepare.test.ts:87-91, 259-333](server/test/auto-prepare.test.ts#L259-L333): four new tests.
- [docs/assisted-apply.md:41-43](docs/assisted-apply.md#L41-L43): rule 12 now describes both behaviours.

### SOLID note

- **Single responsibility, applied.** The SQL lives in the repository, and the policy (when a run may recover, the 30-minute threshold, the wording shown to the owner) lives in the service. That keeps `AutoPrepareService` free of SQL, as it already was.
- **Dependency inversion, kept.** The recovery reads the clock through the existing injectable `now`, so no new dependency was added.
- **Not applied:** a separate "recovery service" or strategy object. It is one call at one place and would add a class without adding a seam anyone needs.

## Verification

- [x] `npm run build`: completed, no warnings (`Application bundle generation complete. [14.331 seconds]`).
- [x] `npm run typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit`, no errors.
- [x] `npm test`: `tests 144, suites 32, pass 144, fail 0`.
- [x] Focused tests in `server/test/auto-prepare.test.ts`. The first two failed before the fix and pass after it:
  - `skips a company that still has an application being prepared or waiting for review from an earlier run` covers a `review` row, a `preparing` row with different case and whitespace in the company name, and a cancelled row, which does not block.
  - `moves an application stuck in preparing for over 30 minutes to failed before counting the queue` checks the status, the note, that `approvedAt` stays null, the audit actor and job, and that no form was opened.
  - `leaves a recent preparing application and every other status exactly as it was` covers a 29-minute `preparing` row plus `review`, `approved`, `previewed`, `needs_attention`, `cancelled`, `submitted` and `failed` rows that are 2 hours old.
  - `recovers nothing while the run is not allowed to go ahead` covers the disabled, kill-switch and setup-unfinished cases.
  - The existing same-run and same-company-gap tests pass unchanged (acceptance criterion 5).

## Manual testing

- Not required for the UI: nothing in the UI changed. A recovered row shows up as an ordinary `failed` application with its note.
- Not run against the owner's live data. Tests use an in-memory database and a fake tailor.

## Risks

- **A draft still really running after 30 minutes would be marked `failed`.** If it then finished, `ApplicationService.prepare` would write `review` over the `failed` status. The result is a usable draft, and the audit log shows both steps. The 30-minute margin makes this unlikely.
- **Pre-existing defect, not fixed here (out of scope: `application-service.ts`).** The "Try again" button on a `failed` application calls `regenerate`, which only accepts `review`/`approved`/`previewed`/`needs_attention` ([application-service.ts:153-154](server/src/services/apply/application-service.ts#L153-L154)). So it answers 409 "Only an unsent application can be regenerated." The recovery note therefore tells the owner to start a new application for the job, which does work. This deserves its own issue.
- **Company-name matching:** SQLite's `lower()` folds only ASCII letters, while the in-run check uses JavaScript's `toLowerCase()`. Two spellings that differ only in the case of a non-ASCII letter would not be treated as the same company by the cross-run check. The existing `lastSubmissionToCompany` query has the same limit.
- **`approved`, `previewed` and `needs_attention` do not block a new draft for the same company.** The issue scoped the check to `preparing` and `review`. An approved but unsent application at a company does not stop a second draft there. Worth deciding in review whether to widen the check.

## Escalation signals

- None.

Closes #14

commit.messageHeadline: chore(apply): start stuck-draft recovery in auto-prepare
fix(apply): recover stuck preparing drafts and skip open-draft companies
commit.messageBody:
An auto-prepare process killed mid-draft left its application in
preparing forever. That row kept counting toward the review queue, so
enough of them made every later run end queue-full with exit code 0.

Each run that is allowed to go ahead now first moves any application
still preparing after 30 minutes to failed, with a note and an
autoprepare.recovered audit entry under the scheduler actor. No other
status is touched.

Candidate selection also skips a company that already has an
application in preparing or review from any earlier run, alongside the
existing same-run and post-submission checks.

Refs issue 14.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
